page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.xlarge is a storage and memory-focused instance within the Local SSDs family, provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. Hardware resources include 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, accompanied by 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per-vCPU ratio. The configuration features an integrated 959 GB local SSD, 35 MB of shared L3 cache, and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware acceleration support includes AVX-512 (f and vnni) and AES instructions, with no discrete GPU hardware installed.

Benchmark evaluations reveal modest compute throughput combined with steady memory access. The processor produces a Geekbench single-core score of 1187.0 and a multi-core score of 2607.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 4274.72. Memory benchmarks demonstrate large-block uncached read speeds of 27.19 GB/sec and write speeds of 23.19 GB/sec, reflected in a Passmark memory score of 2111.59. Application-level metrics record Redis SET execution at 3.49 million operations per second, static web serving throughput at 3.86 GB/sec, and small-model LLM generation speeds of 74.86 tokens per second.

Hardware tradeoffs prioritize local storage capacity and memory density over high compute power or networking bandwidth. The 2 Gbps baseline network connection and 4-thread execution envelope limit its suitability for network-bound services and parallel compilation tasks. However, the bundling of 959 GB local SSD storage alongside 32 GB of memory provides strong resource efficiency for stateful workloads. Recommended use cases include local transactional databases, cache nodes, log ingestion, and intermediate ETL data transformations requiring rapid local disk access.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.xlarge is a storage-oriented instance from the Local SSDs family, provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz. The configuration pairs 32 GB of RAM with a dedicated 959 GB local SSD, delivering a generous 8 GB memory-per-core ratio suited for data-heavy operations. The server supports vector acceleration via AVX-512 and provides a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps, while omitting discrete GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks place its CPU compute performance in lower percentiles, with a Passmark CPU score of 4274.72 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2607.0, balanced by moderate memory execution and 3.49 million Redis SET operations per second. With integrated high-speed local disk storage and elevated memory density relative to vCPU counts, the instance is engineered for transactional databases, caching layers, log aggregation, and local ETL processing pipelines.
